const rm = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

// Scramble
const GLYPHS = "▮§#%&?$@≠*+·";
function scramble(el, text, dur=900){
  if (rm) { el.textContent = text; return; }
  const len = text.length; const start = performance.now();
  function frame(now){
    const p = Math.min(1,(now-start)/dur);
    const settled = Math.floor(p*len);
    let out = text.slice(0, settled);

```js
function scramble(el, text, dur){
  if (rm){ el.textContent = text; return; }
  dur = dur || 900;
  const start = performance.now();
  (function frame(now){
    const p = Math.min(1, (now - start) / dur);
    const settled = Math.floor(p * text.length);
    let out = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++){
      const ch = text[i];
      if (i < settled || ch === " ") out += ch;
      else out += GLYPHS[(Math.random() * GLYPHS.length) | 0];
    }
    el.textContent = out;
    if (p < 1) requestAnimationFrame(frame); else el.textContent = text;
  })(start);
}
```

1. All items are settled in five lines, A.A.B.B.A.
2. 'Bill' may be a man, a beak, a note, or a wave; no two items may be the same Bill, and item 25 may be all of them.
3. The economist (item 03) reserves the right to audit the meter and to bill the Office for doing so. The Office has been billed.
4. Jurgen (item 04) is not liable for any pot, any check, or any burgher.
5. No limerick may end on line four. Line five is the law.
6. The bill (invoice) for this ledger is payable in laughter, on sight, with interest at zero percent."

JS:
```js
const rm = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

// Scramble
const GLYPHS = "▮§#%&?$@≠*+·";
function scramble(el, text, dur=900){
  if (rm) { el.textContent = text; return; }
  const len = text.length; const start = performance.now();
  function frame(now){
    const p = Math.min(1,(now-start)/dur);
    const settled = Math.floor(p*len);
    let out = text.slice(0, settled);
    for(let i=settle... ) out += i< len? (text[i]===' '?' ':GLYPHS[Math.floor(Math.random()*GLYPHS.length)]) : '';
    el.textContent = out;
    if(p<1) requestAnimationFrame(frame); else el.textContent=text;
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
```

01:
There once was a Bill from Limerick
Who took up the task, quite tricky,
Of verse in anapest;
He counted out each beat
And nailed down this very limerick.

02:
There once was a Bill the baker,
A flour-dusted, flour-bearded maker
Of buns and of loaves;
He'd call to the ovens,
"Step up, little cakes — yes, you, my dear baker!"

03:
There was a Bill, the economist,
A graph-poring, currency skeptic
Of markets and yield;
"Each bull run will kneel"
"The bear always wins," he'd say, that economist.

04:
There once was a Bill in the Hamburg
Whom no card trick could ever have stumped —
Until there came Jurgen,
A Hessian burgher,
Who dealt with a grin, and Bill's stack was all trumped.

05:
There once was a Bill the big bell,
A bronze one who rang with a rattle and swell;
No clapper could reach him,
No hammer would teach him,
Yet at half past eleven, he'd ring by himself.

06:
There once was a Bill who'd ring every door,
A bellman who'd wake the whole street and its floor;
"Ring softer, dear Bill!"
The neighbors would call,
But the good man was deaf, and the jingle rang more.

07:
There once was a Bill the bull,
Whose horn was a magnificent, terrible tool;
He'd charge at the farmer,
But never at barley —
For the cows would attest, with a low, that he had a soul.

08:
There once was a Bill with a billhook
And, being of a sentimental blood,
He named the dear iron,
He called it good morning,
"Good day, dear Bill," said he — and the meadow shook.

09:
There once was a Bill the billow,
A wave off a coast where the foam was a mellow yellow;
He'd rise, and he'd crash,
And he'd foam, and he'd splash,
And the fishermen called him "a dear, dear fellow."

10:
There once was a duck named simply Bill,
Who'd sign all his deals with a beak of quill;
No ink, and no nib,
Just a "quack" and a dip
In the pond — and the bank would decline all his will.

11:
There once was a Bill the billed lark
Whose bill of fare was four thousand songs from the park;
He'd sing them all through,
Then sing them again, new —
And faint in the field, and the meadow was dark.

12:
There once was a Bill who was the fifth
(A dollar), who'd travel with a wonderful drift
Through every tip cup,
And every register,
And think he was worth much more than his self.

13:
There once was a Bill the billfold,
A pocket of paper families of bills;
They'd fan out, all crisp,
When he'd tap his wrist:
"Good morning, my bills, and the whole village — no spills."

14:
There once was a Bill the billboard,
Who'd holler out "SALE!" with the whole of his cord;
"LOST CAT — REWARD,"
Then "VOTE — ONE WORD,"
Then a quiet "BILL," which the drivers adored.

15:
There once was a Bill the willow
Who'd dress, all year round, in a mellow yellow;
He'd dip in the stream
To comb out the cream,
And the ducks would go by, "Good morning, dear fellow."

16:
There once was a Bill the pillow,
Who'd keep dreams in a mellow little hollow;
He'd be pressed, and he'd sigh,
Then whisper, "Good-by —
I'll hold them all till the morning is yellow."

17:
There once was a Bill who'd bill out the rain,
And the cloud, and the drizzle, and sky, nook by nook:

JS:
```js
const rm = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

// Scramble
const GLYPHS = "▮§#%&?$@≠*+·";
function scramble(el, text, dur=900){
  if (rm) { el.textContent = text; return; }
  const len = text.length; const start = performance.now();
  function frame(now){
    const p = Math.min(1,(now-start)/dur);
    const settled = Math.floor(p*len);
    let out = text.slice(0, settled);
    for(let i=settle... ) out += i< len? (text[i]===' '?' ':GLYPHS[Math.floor(Math.random()*GLYPHS.length)]) : '';
    el.textContent = out;
    if(p<1) requestAnimationFrame(frame); else el.textContent=text;
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
```

function scramble(el, text, dur){

  dur = dur || 900;

}
